title: A failing migration rolls back its own transaction and the runner exits non-zero without advancing schema_version
asA: operator running migrations at boot on a long-lived Node process
iWant: a failing migration to roll back its own transaction and stop the runner with a non-zero exit and the failing filename in the diagnostic
soThat: the runner never leaves a partially-applied migration on the database and the operator can name the failing file to un-jam the deploy

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a migrations directory whose second file contains an invalid SQL statement (simulated in the fixture by the SIMULATE_MIGRATION_FAILURE switch), when the migration runner runs, then the first file commits, the second file's transaction rolls back on the invalid statement, the runner exits non-zero, and the failing filename appears in the runner's diagnostic output. The schema_version bookkeeping table records only the first file's row.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Postgres at schema_version 0 and three migration files where the second is intentionally broken
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migration runner applies the directory with SIMULATE_MIGRATION_FAILURE=true
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first file's transaction commits and its row lands in the bookkeeping table; the second file's transaction rolls back; the runner exits non-zero with the failing filename in its stderr; the third file is not attempted; the bookkeeping table shows exactly one applied row
